1: You are the dragon today. Not the knight, not the princess. Put on the scales and wait to be addressed as Great.
2: Be the mare, and don't steer. Become the weather the carriage is driving into. Pack a bag for the south-west and a eulogy for the north-east.
3: Your first night on stage the wig will be crooked and the microphone will die. Stay. Appoint a friend to hold the wig.
4: A beginner asks you the same question three times. Answer once, with your whole face. After that, hand them a mop and let the floor explain.
5: You are waiting for the thing, and the thing is parking. Order a drink. Hold it like you were invited.
6: You are in the right, which is a poor place to live. Move out. See someone enormous and leave the argument in the hall with its shoes on.
7: Raise an army, but run it like a drag house: a mother, matching names, glitter on everything that could cause injury.
8: Stand close to the ones who stand close back. First turn out your pockets; there's a stone in there for every grudge. Latecomers get the cold dumplings.
9: The clouds are in position and have said nothing. Be the sky: look like you might, and don't.
10: You stepped on the tiger's tail and it only looked at you, like a bouncer. Compliment its shoes and go in.
11: The small thing is leaving by the back door as the big thing arrives by the front. Hold both doors. Introduce no one.
12: Everyone is talking and nobody is being heard: a long party at the wrong address. Stop explaining. Go home early with the leftovers.
13: Gather outside, in daylight, with the unvetted. Fellowship that only works in a basement has not yet earned the sun.
14: You have inherited the sun. It came with debts and a cat. Feed the cat; skip the paperwork.
15: Be so modest that it becomes a kind of glamour. Wear sunglasses to your own coronation and let everyone watch you not mention it.
16: Someone put a record on and now the whole town is a dance floor. Go with it. It was the bass's idea.
17: Follow something that has no idea it is leading: a parade, a bridal train, a pigeon in good shoes. Keep your name out of it.
18: The leftovers have started a political movement. Learn their demands, then dispose of them with ceremony over three days.
19: A great thing is approaching on small, brisk feet. In eight months it will want something. Prepare a face for that day.
20: Hands washed, offering still in your pocket. Stand in the doorway until the room wonders what you're carrying. Let them guess, then be magnificent about it.
21: There is a bone in the meal and it is the truth. Bite down. The dentist is a distant cousin and will understand.
22: Add glitter, but only to the things that can take it. A thing that is all decoration is a hat looking for a head.
23: It's all coming off, like wallpaper, like a wig in a gale. Don't paste. Stand under the falling and see what you look like with nothing on the walls.
24: You are a bad habit returning with a new haircut. Seven days. The door was never locked, only polite.
25: Behave in a crowd the way you behave in the shower. Anyone who objects is in the wrong shower.
26: Stop eating at your mother's. Cook for yourself, in public, with the windows open. The great river is out front with someone's boat attached.
27: Watch what feeds you: a meal, a friend, a rumour. The mouth you are ashamed of is hungry for a poem. Serve one.
28: The ridgepole is bowing, showgirl-style. Leave it be, and leave by any direction at all, in the dress.
29: Fall in. Bring a snack. The abyss has waited ages for good company and will teach you the sea by being extremely rude.
30: Be a flame with the temperament of a cow. Burn slowly, towards grass, and take it personally when no one stands near.
31: Touch what attracts you the way a moth reads a menu: with the whole body, without a plan. If there is a wedding, the moth officiates.
32: Do the strange thing every day until it becomes a heritage. Whichever way you walk is now tradition.
33: Leave the party at its height, as rumours do. Take your coat, your friends, and one of the good spoons.
34: You are enormous and correct, a combination considered unsafe indoors. Go up the stairs like a piano, slowly, with several people shouting directions.
35: You've been given many horses and seen three times in one day. Accept them, name each after an ex, and do not ride the third.
36: The sun has gone into the wardrobe. Sit in the dark and glitter anyway; sequins bring their own light.
37: A household runs on whoever holds it together. Find out who that is and give them a title, a crown and the good chair.
38: You and your opposite stand back to back, pointing at the same moon. Small things will work. Don't hold a summit; hold hands, awkwardly.
39: The road has gone lame. Go south-west, away from what you keep calling north-east. Visit someone elderly and extremely well dressed.
40: The knot lets go, bad marriage and all. If nothing is left to do, lie on the floor. If something is, do it before lunch, in better shoes.
41: Subtract until two bowls of rice are a banquet. Serve them as though the whole sea had been folded into the bowls.
42: Everything you touch gets a little more of itself, you included. Touch recklessly. Cross the water.
43: Name the offender in the town square, in your good coat, then quietly in the kitchen. Skip the war; send a loud and beautifully formatted letter.
44: A creature walks in that has never once been furniture. Don't wed it. Offer soup, a door, and your phone number, and see what it takes.
45: Gather at the shrine, and bring the ones nobody sat. Make a real offering. Every direction is permitted; some are more fabulous.
46: Grow like a tree that has been told a secret. Rise slowly, southward. When you reach the great person, be in the middle of a sentence.
47: You are in a dry well with an opinion. Speak less; words aren't currency down here. Barter with a hat.
48: Towns move and the well stays. Draw from it, and do not break the bucket on the last inch, which is the longest one.
49: Nothing is true until the glitter lands, and then everyone will say they always knew. Let them. Change your name in the mirror first.
50: The cauldron is the size of a small cathedral and bubbling. Great success. Don't look in; hand out spoons.
51: Thunder arrives and a hundred miles of people drop their drinks. You, ladle in hand, keep stirring.
52: Sit like a mountain with your back to everybody. Cross the courtyard and see no one; no one sees you. That was the whole performance.
53: The goose arrives in stages: rock, tree, roof. Arrive at your marriage the same way, in stages, with luggage and a vow written in glitter.
54: Any move today is a mistake, a veil in a swimming pool. Make it only if the story will be better than the mistake.
55: Be the sun at noon: no shadows, no notes, no apology. The afternoon has its own job.
56: Travel light and be polite to strangers, who are mostly sequins in a coat. A small success is waiting in a doorway. Carry only what can be sung.
57: Be the draught under the door. Go any direction, change one small thing in every room, and visit the elder, who will pretend not to notice.
58: Talk and laugh with your whole face. It is correct. Let nobody tidy it.
59: Scatter like glitter in a taxi. For weeks you will be found in unexpected places. Cross the water as a rumour.
60: A rule that hurts to follow is a hat that is too small. Unpick it and make it a hat for somebody else.
61: Be so sincere that pigs and fish are moved. Test it on the nearest pig. Cross the water with a full heart and a cold sandwich.
62: Do small things loudly and leave the big thing alone. A bird's song falls rather than rises; be a bird who has accepted gravity.
63: You finished, and now there is chaos in the pantry. This is the usual order of things. Keep one eye on the ending, which is looking back.
64: The fox gets her tail wet at the very last step, and so do you. Good: a dry tail is a lie. Be the soggy hero.
